EL4-F-01.hint: The argument of a logarithm must be positive. Set the argument greater than \(0\) and solve; the boundary is the vertical asymptote. The range of a logarithmic function is all real numbers.
slips: Using the wrong direction after a reflection. For \(-x+c>0\), you get \(x<c\).
Giving a restricted range. A vertical shift or reflection does not change the range of a logarithm.

EL4-A-01.hint: For an \(x\)-intercept, set \(f(x)=0\) and rewrite in exponential form. To find a value, choose an input that makes the argument a power of the base.
slips: Writing the \(x\)-intercept as \(x=b^{-k}\) and forgetting to add back the shift.
Using an input outside the domain.

parts.q: State the domain in interval notation.
parts.a: The argument must be positive: \(x - 2 \gt  0\), so \(x \gt  2\). The domain is \((2, \infty)\).

parts.q: State the range in interval notation.
parts.a: \((-\infty, \infty)\). A vertical shift or a reflection does not change the range of a logarithmic function.

parts.q: Give the equation of the vertical asymptote.
parts.a: \(x = 2\), the boundary of the domain.
